reading.title: Warmer homes, lower bills
reading.text: Energy prices have a direct effect on household budgets, and rising costs affect poorer families most. One of the most effective responses is not new power stations but more efficient homes. Insulating walls and roofs can cut heating bills by a third. Experts say the key factor is cost: many families cannot afford the work upfront, so some governments now offer loans that are repaid through the savings. Poorly built homes with defects such as damp walls can also harm health, increasing the risk of infections.
